transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-10 | Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood CSM), Dr. Elena Kwan (NovaThera Head of ML), Ravi Menon (Platform), Lisa Ortiz (Procurement), Omar Castillo (SRE)
---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can we do a quick intro?
[00:05] Elena: Hi, Elena here. Good afternoon.
[00:06] Ravi: Ravi — platform engineering, hello.
[00:08] Lisa: Lisa, procurement.
[00:10] Omar: Omar, SRE.
[00:12] Sofia: Great. Marcus, Hannah, wanna do a one-liner?
[00:14] Marcus: Marcus Li, Redwood SE — I'll lead the benchmark and technical side.
[00:17] Hannah: Hannah Reyes, CSM — I'll track the ops long lead items and help with the doc handoff.
[00:20] Sofia: Cool, high level agenda: usage & cost trends, root cause for the July spike, reliability incidents and mitigations, and then dedicated/vpc questions plus next steps.
[00:30] Elena: Sounds good. We want the session to focus on whether Dedicated is worth it for us and timeline for VPC. Also, we need to understand the cost tradeoffs — we saw a big spike in mid-July that surprised finance.
[00:45] Sofia: Yep, we'll cover that. Marcus, can you walk through the usage profile we've been seeing versus the committed capacity?
[00:50] Marcus: Sure — so, from Redwood console logs — and I'm paraphrasing here — NovaThera saw a sustained increase in token output from July 10 to July 16. Avg tokens-per-request jumped from ~430 to ~1,200 for a handful of routes, likely due to a long-tail generation change in your pipeline. There was also a pattern of concurrent long sequences hitting the hosted pool which pushed up burst provisioning and egress.
[01:20] Ravi: That matches our telemetry. We had a model change in prod — a context-expansion for the summarization route — and we didn't throttle it. It was a config rollout mistake.
[01:34] Sofia: Ok — so root cause is a rollout + lack of guarding. Two quick notes: Optimize has suggestions for prefix caching and our batching knobs; also Dedicated gives you reserved capacity which flattens that burst cost. But Dedicated is a commitment.
[01:55] Elena: That's the core question — finance wants to know if Dedicated is worth the committed spend versus improving throttles and batching. Any numbers to show?
[02:05] Marcus: Preliminary: if you were on Dedicated sized for your 95th percentile, the per-token unit cost drops by ~20-30% depending on quantization and batch sizes. But that doesn't account for developer velocity or the one-off cadence changes. I'll run a more exact cost-sim after we get your sequence length histogram.
[02:30] Lisa: From procurement, we'd like to see both a conservative and aggressive scenario. Also, what are the fiscal terms for burst overage on Dedicated?
[02:40] Hannah: We have two burst models: capped burst (additional fee per GPU hour) and timed burst (short windows at no extra charge up to X). I'll add the exact contract language in the doc we send.
[02:52] Sofia: On reliability: Omar, you flagged two 5xx spikes during that week — can you describe incident impact?
[02:58] Omar: Yeah, we had two 10–15 minute blips where customers experienced timeouts on the summarization endpoint. The app switched to a degraded path but customers saw higher latency. Our alerting caught it but we didn't have automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant.
[03:15] Marcus: Right — Redwood Console supports fallback rules (policy: latency-first or cost-first). We can define automatic routing to a smaller quantized variant when latency/SLOs degrade. We should test the fallback logic in the canary.
[03:30] Elena: Important: we cannot have output quality regressions. Any rerouting must preserve acceptable quality.
[03:36] Marcus: Understood — we can include a set of prompt-based evals and thresholds so fallback only happens if generated score is within acceptable delta. We'll run side-by-side evaluation during the canary.
[03:50] Sofia: On security/compliance: Lisa — what do you need to see for Private/VPC evaluation?
[03:55] Lisa: SOC2, KMS/HSM details, audit log retention, SSO/SAML details, and data residency statements if we move to an EU region. Also vendor risk questionnaire.
[04:10] Hannah: We'll share the SOC2 package and KMS integration spec. Redwood Private supports customer KMS via external KMS, and we can provide audit log schemas. I'll attach them after this call.
[04:22] Omar: For VPC, we need an ingress/egress topology diagram — how requests route, what IP ranges, and whether private peering is an option.
[04:30] Marcus: We'll include the network diagrams. For on-prem or air-gapped, that's more involved — we can scope it if you need but it's usually a separate engagement.
[04:42] Elena: Timeline: our legal wants to finish procurement by end of September. We need pilot in August to inform that decision.
[04:52] Sofia: Ok let's aim for a two-week canary starting Aug 24 — tentative. Marcus, you'll run the benchmark with Rafael's harness? (Note: mis-typed name, but internal reference)
[04:59] Marcus: Yep, I'll partner with Ravi on the harness. We need the sample prompt set and expected throughput targets.
[05:07] Ravi: I'll export the traffic profile and the long-seq histogram this week. Expect that by Friday.
[05:12] Lisa: On pricing, please include both per-token and committed GPU hour models and an example monthly P&L for our current traffic plus a +50% growth scenario.
[05:24] Marcus: Quick tech note: quantization changes can reduce memory and increase batch sizes — we'll try int8 for non-critical routes and measure latency impact. That could drop unit cost substantially but we need to validate quality.
[05:38] Elena: What about KV cache and prefix caching? Could that have prevented the spike?
[05:42] Marcus: Potentially. If many requests shared large context prefixes we can cache key-value states to reduce repeated compute. Optimize can recommend which routes benefit most. We'll surface those suggestions in the cost-sim.
[05:56] Omar: For the incident triage cadence — can we set a weekly 30-min triage for the next month? We'll want to watch error budgets and any re-rollouts.
[06:05] Hannah: Yes, I'll schedule a standing 30-min Wednesday slot for four weeks starting Aug 12; will invite the SREs and product owners.
[06:15] Lisa: Procurement question: if we go Dedicated, what's the minimum commitment term?
[06:20] Sofia: Typically 3 or 12 months. Short-term committed windows have higher unit price. We'll include both options with modeled economics.
[06:28] Elena: We also want a playbook for rollouts to avoid the previous mistake — rollout gates, canary percentage floor, and automated throttles.
[06:36] Marcus: We'll propose a rollout template: start at 1% with traffic shaping, autoscaling cap, and automated rollback on quality metrics. We'll run through it in the canary.
[06:46] Sofia: Anything else on compliance?
[06:48] Lisa: Just one more — can Redwood support customer-managed KMS key rotation cadence documentation? We have strict rotation policies.
[06:55] Hannah: We support rotation. I'll include the rotation cadence and HSM-backed key notes in the KMS doc.
[07:02] Sofia: OK, let's do a quick recap and assign owners.
[07:06] Marcus: I'll run the cost-sim and bench plan once Ravi's traffic profile is in.
[07:10] Ravi: I'll share the histogram and throughput targets by Friday 08/14.
[07:14] Lisa: Procurement will review the conservative and aggressive pricing templates once Sofia sends them.
[07:18] Omar: I'll confirm SRE availability for the canary and share the on-call Slack channel.
[07:22] Sofia: Great — we'll send the SOC2 pack and KMS notes by 08/12, pricing by 08/13, and schedule the canary for Aug 24 start pending confirmations.
[07:30] Elena: One quick question — any mention of competitor lock-in if we go Dedicated? Finance is worried about switching costs.
[07:36] Sofia: Good question. Redwood Dedicated keeps the same API and model catalog; migration back to Hosted is supported but may require data-plane changes depending on VPC. We'll document rollback and exit strategies.
[07:48] Marcus: Also we'll ensure we record model versions and prompt sets in the rollout so you can reproduce outputs on a different infra if needed.
[07:58] Lisa: That helps. Procurement will want that in writing.
[08:03] Sofia: Cool. Any final questions?
[08:05] Elena: No, thanks. This is helpful.
[08:07] Sofia: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts. Meeting end.
---
